abstract: We study principal component analysis when the dimension d is much larger than the sample size n under an independent-factor sub-Gaussian model. The dual sample covariance is decomposed into a finite-rank score matrix, an isotropic bulk shift, and a high-probability remainder governed by the bulk trace τ_0, Frobenius scale q_0, and largest noise eigenvalue b_0 = ||Λ_0||_{op}. This decomposition separates fixed-score HDLSS limits from joint limits in which n also grows. It shows that sequential noise reduction generally targets a score oracle containing a later-spike subtraction, while an oracle block correction avoids that subtraction when the signal rank is known. A parallel cross-data-matrix bound explains the benefit and cost of sample splitting. Reproducible Gaussian-factor simulations with 1,000 replications per configuration confirm the score-oracle approximation, the multi-spike subtraction, the separation between eigenvalue and eigenvector scales, and the population transition when n grows.
